title: How to Store Carrots and Celery in Water So They Stay Insanely Crisp for 4 Weeks
description: Stop throwing away limp veggies! Here is how to store carrots and celery in water to keep them crunchy and fresh for up to a full month of holiday cooking.
story: I used to be the queen of discovering sad, rubbery carrots in the back of my apartment fridge's crisper drawer right when I needed to chop mirepoix for Thanksgiving stuffing. Paying $4.50 at the corner bodega for emergency replacement celery because mine turned to mush made my frugal heart ache, especially when a 2-pound bag is under $1.50 at Aldi. Last November, determined not to waste a single cent or scrap during holiday prep, I started submerging pre-cut carrot and celery sticks in wide-mouth jars of cold water. The first time I tested this, I sealed the lid airtight without changing the water for ten days—big mistake, it got cloudy and weird. Once I learned to swap out fresh water twice a week, they stayed snap-crackingly crisp for over a month. It saved my holiday budget, my sanity, and zero veggies got tossed.
ingredients: 2 large bunches fresh celery (trimmed and washed)
2 lbs whole carrots (peeled or scrubbed clean)
6 to 8 cups cold filtered water (enough to submerge veggies)
Clean kitchen towel or paper towels (for drying prior to cooking)
instructions: Trim and wash: Slice off the white base and leafy tops of the celery stalks (freeze tops for chicken stock later). Peel carrots if desired, or scrub clean under cold water.
Cut into batons: Slice carrots and celery ribs into uniform 3- to 4-inch sticks that fit vertically inside a 32-ounce wide-mouth mason jar with about an inch of space below the rim.
Pack and submerge: Stand the veggie sticks upright in the clean glass jars. Pour cold filtered water straight over them until every single stick is completely submerged.
Seal and chill: Screw the jar lids on and place them on a middle fridge shelf where temperatures stay stable (skip the fridge door, which swings warm).
The 3-day water swap: Every 3 to 4 days, dump the soaking liquid, rinse the sticks under the tap, and refill with fresh cold water to maintain peak snap for up to 4 weeks.
proHack: If your store-bought celery is already starting to bend, trim 1/4-inch off the bottom and stand the stalks in a glass of ice-cold tap water for 30 minutes on the counter before cutting; they will drink up moisture and stiffen right back up.
storage: Keep jars on a middle or bottom fridge shelf at 35°F to 38°F. Never freeze in water jars, as the expanding liquid will crack the glass. Before roasting or sautéing, thoroughly pat the vegetables dry with a clean kitchen towel so they caramelize instead of steam.

faqs.question: Can I substitute mason jars if I don't have them?
faqs.answer: Yes! Any tall, food-safe plastic container, glass pyrex dish, or thoroughly cleaned repurposed pickle jar works. Just make sure the vessel is tall enough to keep the vegetables fully submerged in water.

faqs.question: How do I prevent the water from turning cloudy or slimy?
faqs.answer: Cloudiness happens when natural starches leach out or tiny bacteria multiply. Prevent this by rinsing your cut sticks before jarring and swapping in clean, cold water every 3 to 4 days without skipping.
